## What

Add an `issue-fleet` skill that turns the main session into an **orchestrator** running a fleet of
subagents, each working a different open issue in its own git worktree, plus the two host tools that
make the selection and the budgeting real rather than re-derived by prose every run.

The tracker has 64 open issues and 19 of them already carry a written `## Implementation plan`
comment — prior work sitting idle — but there is no way to work more than one at a time.
`.claude/worktrees/` exists and is empty.

Owner requirements: target the highest-impact issues, prioritise issues with prior work already
done, choose the batch so parallel workers are unlikely to touch the same files, delegate to cheaper
models aggressively without compromising code quality, and respect a not-to-exceed usage ceiling on
the 5-hour and weekly limits.

Deliverables:

- `.agents/skills/issue-fleet/SKILL.md` + `references/worker-brief.md`
- `host/tools/fleet_plan.py` — issue scoring, file-footprint extraction and expansion, conflict-free
  batch selection
- `host/tools/fleet_budget.py` — rolling 5h/168h usage estimate against an owner-declared ceiling
- `host/src/roomscan/mcp_server/tools_fleet.py` exposing both as MCP tools
- `.claude/agents/fleet-worker.md` (sonnet) and `fleet-worker-mech.md` (haiku)

Three measured findings drive the design:

1. **Subagent token spend is persisted at `~/.claude/projects/<proj>/<session-uuid>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl`**
   — nested one level below the main transcripts. A flat `projects/*/*.jsonl` glob misses 100% of it.
   Today that is only 2.8% of output tokens because subagents are barely used here; a fleet inverts
   that ratio, so the budget tool must prove its glob covers the nested path and report `coverage`.
2. **The median extractable file footprint per issue is one file** (51/64 issues have at least one
   tracked path). Intersecting raw footprints declares nearly every pair conflict-free, so footprints
   must be expanded via a co-edit graph built from `git log --name-only` before conflict is computed.
3. **The collisions that actually bite are not files** — the single shared Playwright browser in the
   MCP server, port 8000, the rig/SWD probe, and the GPU. Those need an explicit per-wave resource
   cap orthogonal to file footprints.

Also amends the standing rule "subagents don't commit; the controlling session commits" (stated in
both `docs/engineering-practices.md` and `status-sync`) with a fleet carve-out: workers commit
`Refs #NNN` on their own branch inside their own worktree, and the orchestrator reviews, rebases,
fast-forwards to `main`, and writes the single closing commit.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `fleet_plan()` returns a conflict-free batch against the live tracker, ranked with prior-work
      weighting, with per-issue footprint, confidence tier, resources and suggested model tier
- [ ] Two `area/host-web` issues that both reach `index.html` only after co-edit expansion are never
      co-scheduled (the regression test for the whole selection design)
- [ ] `fleet_budget()` reports a non-empty `limit_basis` on every return path, computes a rolling
      168h window locally, and returns `verdict: "unknown"` rather than a number on any failure
- [ ] `fleet_budget()`'s transcript reader is proven to match the nested `*/subagents/*.jsonl` path
- [ ] Both scripts are registered as MCP tools and listed in `EXPOSED` in
      `host/tests/test_mcp_registry.py` and in `docs/mcp-server.md`
- [ ] The subagent-commit carve-out lands in `docs/engineering-practices.md` and `status-sync`
- [ ] A live dry run completes one full round trip on a real low-risk issue: claim → worktree →
      spawn → review → rebase → `merge --ff-only` → worktree removal → close
- [ ] Tests green

  and **worst-case** statistics displayed inline; (c) add a **Reset Stats** button to
  zero the worst-case counters. Reduces scroll burden on the dock band while improving

## Implementation plan

### Metric semantics

* Treat **worst-case** as the highest observed p95 jitter since the last reset—not the largest pose angle, since normal scanner movement would make that meaningless.
* Stream bars show `host_hz / device_hz`, matching the existing desktop HUD.
* Sensor bars show:

  * Roll: signed range ±180°
  * Tilt: signed range ±90°
  * Heading: 0–360°
  * Fusion correction: signed range ±180°
* Keep peak statistics server-owned so all connected tabs share the same reset baseline.

### Implementation

1. **Expose fusion correction**

   * Add a read-only correction accessor to `YawFusion` and `SensorState` in `host/src/roomscan/sensors.py`.
   * Add `fusion_correction_deg` to the additive `sensor` WebSocket payload in `host/src/roomscan/web.py`.
   * Extend `OrientationJitter` with a `fusion` signal so correction jitter uses the same full-precision, server-side calculation as roll, tilt, and heading.

2. **Track resettable worst-case jitter**

   * Extend `OrientationJitter` to retain each signal’s maximum p95 value since reset.
   * Extend `RateMeter`/`StreamRate` in `host/src/roomscan/metrics.py` with peak stream jitter.
   * Add reset methods that clear only peak values; rolling live statistics continue uninterrupted.
   * Add a `reset_stats` WebSocket command that resets both registries and logs the action. Cleared peaks should render as `—` until a fresh measurement arrives rather than fabricating a measured zero.

3. **Rebuild the Sensors card**

   * Replace the flat Roll/Tilt/Heading/Fusion rows in `host/src/roomscan/static/index.html` with a compact 2×2 `.sensor-metric-grid`.
   * Each tile contains the editable label, current value, horizontal bar, current p95 jitter, and worst p95 jitter.
   * Preserve the orientation gizmo, compass, warnings, fusion status/remedy, environment section, existing controls, and full diagnostic values.
   * Keep Yaw and overall-orientation jitter in Diagnostics; add the fusion signal and worst column there for complete inspection.

4. **Upgrade Stream rows**

   * Update `host/src/roomscan/static/hud.js` so every sensor stream renders a delivery-ratio bar plus inline host rate, current jitter, and worst jitter.
   * Use the existing good-high thresholds: green at ≥90%, amber at 70–90%, and red below 70%.
   * Render an empty track when `device_hz` is unavailable.
   * Keep the existing bandwidth, Drops, and Gaps displays unchanged.

5. **Add Reset Stats**

   * Add one `Reset Stats` button to the Stream card with the required plain-language `title`.
   * Send `reset_stats`; let subsequent server messages drive both cards so reconnects and multiple tabs remain consistent.
   * Do not reuse `Reset Heading`: fusion-filter reset and telemetry-baseline reset remain separate actions.

6. **Document the additive JSON changes**

   * Update `docs/web-protocol.md` with `fusion_correction_deg`, per-signal `worst_p95_deg`, per-stream `worst_jitter_ms`, and `reset_stats`.
   * No firmware or binary protocol version change is required.

### Tests and verification

* `host/tests/test_sensors.py`: correction accessor and fusion-reset behavior.
* `host/tests/test_web.py`: sensor serialization, fusion jitter, peak retention/reset, and `reset_stats` dispatch.
* `host/tests/test_metrics.py`: stream peak tracking, monotonic maximum behavior, and reset.
* `host/tests/test_static_ui.py`: required IDs, tooltips, 2×2 structure, and progress-bar markup.
* Run the full host pytest suite.
* Use the repository’s headless browser workflow with replay data to verify:

  * the open Sensors card fits the dock without wrapping or auto-collapse;
  * bars and statistics update from real messages;
  * peaks persist after the rolling window changes;
  * Reset Stats clears both cards and new peaks accumulate afterward;
  * desktop and narrow viewport screenshots remain usable.

### Acceptance criteria

* Sensors presents Roll, Tilt, Heading, and Fusion Correction in a readable 2×2 grid.
* Every sensor tile and stream row has a working progress bar, live jitter, and resettable worst-case jitter.
* Reset Stats affects every connected client through server-owned state.
* Existing sensor controls, warnings, diagnostics, stream loss counters, and SLAM inputs are unchanged.
* The Sensors card’s measured open height is reduced from the current baseline and remains inside the dock band at the documented 1000 px test viewport.

## Implementation plan

Move the replay transport controls out of the Secondary sidebar and into a dedicated floating, video-player-style panel at the bottom of the 3D viewport.

### 1. Extract playback markup from the sidebar

In `host/src/roomscan/static/index.html`:

- Remove the current `#transport-card` control-group from the Secondary sidebar.
- Add a dedicated `#playback-panel` outside both sidebars, over the 3D viewport.
- Preserve the existing control IDs so the transport protocol and event wiring do not need to change:
  - `btn-golive`
  - `btn-playpause`
  - `btn-transport-restart`
  - `seg-speed`
  - `chk-loop`
  - `seek`
  - `pos-status`
- Reorganize them horizontally like a media player:
  - restart + play/pause on the left
  - seek bar and current/duration/frame status in the center
  - speed + loop + Go Live on the right
- Keep the panel hidden unless replay is active.

### 2. Add dedicated floating-panel styling

Also in `index.html`'s existing component styles:

- Add `.playback-panel` styles rather than inheriting `.sidebar .control-group`.
- Position it `fixed` and centered horizontally near the bottom of the usable 3D viewport.
- Anchor its bottom position from `--dock-bottom` so expanding/collapsing the Event Log cannot cover it.
- Give it the same glass/card visual language as the rest of the UI, but use a compact horizontal layout appropriate for transport controls.
- Add a sensible max width and responsive wrapping/compaction for narrow windows.
- Keep the seek bar as the dominant flexible element.
- Make all controls pointer-interactive without interfering with OrbitControls outside the panel.

The panel should remain visually distinct from the full-width Event Log underneath it.

### 3. Decouple Playback from sidebar/card-collapse behavior

`layout.js` currently treats `data-card-id="transport"` as a normal persistent/collapsible card.

Since the new playback panel is transient replay chrome rather than a sidebar card:

- Remove `transport` from sidebar/card-collapse-specific icon/title/default-state bookkeeping where it is no longer applicable.
- Do not give the new panel `data-card-id="transport"`.
- Ensure it is not affected by sidebar visibility, sidebar resizing, squircle/card restoration, or persisted `roomscan.card.transport.collapsed` state.
- Keep using the existing `--dock-bottom` measurement produced by `layout.js` to avoid the Event Log.

This also means hiding the Secondary sidebar must no longer hide playback controls.

### 4. Update `capture.js` without changing transport semantics

In `host/src/roomscan/static/capture.js`:

- Replace the `transportCard` DOM reference with the new `playbackPanel`.
- Continue driving visibility exclusively from:
  `session.playback.is_replay`
- Preserve the existing one-way server-state flow for:
  - pause/resume
  - restart
  - playback speed
  - loop
  - seek
  - Go Live
- Preserve the current seek behavior where `input` previews locally while dragging and `change` commits the seek.
- Preserve `pos-status` formatting and server-driven active states.

No backend/WebSocket protocol changes should be necessary.

### 5. Update layout/default-state tests

There are tests which currently treat `transport` as a normal collapsible card/default layout entry.

Update those expectations so Playback is no longer part of the sidebar-card state model.

Add/static-check coverage that:

- the playback panel exists outside `#secondary-bar`
- the old `#transport-card` sidebar card is gone
- all existing transport control IDs still exist exactly once

### 6. Headless UI regression

Using the existing replay/headless-Chrome workflow from `docs/web-ui-testing.md`:

1. Start against a replay capture.
2. Assert `#playback-panel` is visible.
3. Assert its bounding box is:
   - horizontally inside the viewport
   - above the Event Log
   - outside the Secondary sidebar DOM
4. Exercise the real controls:
   - pause and resume
   - restart
   - 0.5× / 1× / 2× / Max
   - loop
   - seek
5. Confirm `#pos-status` advances/updates as expected.
6. Toggle the Secondary sidebar off and confirm the playback panel remains visible and usable.
7. Expand the Event Log and confirm the panel moves/stays above it rather than overlapping it.
8. Take screenshots at desktop and narrow viewport widths to verify the player remains usable without covering important sidebar controls.

### Acceptance criteria

- Playback controls are no longer present in the Secondary sidebar.
- A replay displays one floating playback panel at the bottom of the 3D viewport.
- The panel contains seek, play/pause, restart, speed, loop, position/status, and Go Live controls.
- Existing playback behavior and WebSocket messages are unchanged.
- The panel only appears during replay.
- Sidebar hide/resize/collapse state does not affect the panel.
- The Event Log cannot overlap the panel.
- Existing transport controls remain fully operable in headless UI testing.
- No duplicate transport element IDs are introduced.

### Expected files

- `host/src/roomscan/static/index.html`
- `host/src/roomscan/static/capture.js`
- `host/src/roomscan/static/layout.js`
- relevant assertions in `host/tests/test_web.py`
- `docs/web-ui-testing.md` only if selector/documentation references need updating

No firmware or backend transport changes should be required.

# BUG-096 — Oscillate orbit mode non-functional and slider always enabled

**Date filed:** 2026-08-08  
**Status:** open  
**Area:** host/web UI (View panel, camera controls)  

## Summary

The "Oscillate" orbit mode toggle in the View panel does nothing — enabling oscillation produces no visible camera motion. Additionally, the oscillation amplitude slider remains enabled regardless of whether oscillate mode is active; it should be disabled when oscillate mode is off.

## Observation

- The Oscillate toggle control exists and responds to clicks
- No camera oscillation occurs when toggled on
- The oscillation amplitude slider is always interactive, even when oscillate mode is disabled
- The slider should be visually and functionally disabled (grayed out, non-interactive) when oscillate mode is off

## Expected behavior

1. When Oscillate is toggled **on**: the camera should autonomously oscillate (triangle wave ±N degrees) about the current azimuth
2. When Oscillate is toggled **off**: the camera should hold a fixed azimuth without oscillation
3. The oscillation amplitude slider should only be enabled/interactive when Oscillate mode is active

## Root cause

Unknown. Suspected areas:
- The oscillate-mode state is not being passed to the camera controller / SLAM orbit logic
- The orbit oscillation is not being applied in the scene's animation loop
- The slider's disabled state is not being bound to the oscillate toggle's state in the UI

## Resolution

TBD — requires inspection of the orbit camera logic in `slam.js`, the View panel's oscillate control binding, and the connection between the UI state and the animation loop.

---

comments.body:
## Implementation plan

The existing oscillation math is already present in `scene.js`; this looks primarily like a UI/state-wiring bug.

### Current behavior / likely root cause

- `host/src/roomscan/static/scene.js`
  - Already implements `updateOscillate()` as a triangle wave.
  - `isOscillating()` requires all three conditions:
    - `orbit_enabled`
    - `orbit_mode === "oscillate"`
    - `view_mode === "world"`
  - The render loop already calls `updateOscillate()` immediately before `controls.update(dt)`.

- `host/src/roomscan/static/controls.js`
  - Clicking **Oscillate** currently sends only:
    `orbit_mode: "oscillate"`
  - Auto-orbit defaults to disabled, so selecting Oscillate by itself can leave `orbit_enabled === false`, making `isOscillating()` false and producing no camera motion.
  - The amplitude slider is currently disabled only when leaving World mode; it remains enabled in Continuous mode and while orbit is stopped.

- `host/src/roomscan/web.py`
  - Already accepts and persists `orbit`, `orbit_mode`, and `orbit_amplitude` together, so no protocol redesign should be necessary.

### Changes

1. **Make selecting Oscillate actually start oscillation**
   - Update the `seg-orbit-mode` handler in `controls.js`.
   - When the user selects `oscillate`, send `orbit_mode: "oscillate"` and `orbit: true` in the same `set_view` message.
   - Keep the existing Auto-orbit checkbox as the master start/stop control so the user can pause the motion without losing the selected mode/amplitude.

2. **Keep mode changes atomic**
   - Rely on the existing server state echo rather than locally mutating checkbox/button state.
   - This keeps multiple browser tabs synchronized and preserves the current one-way state-flow convention.

3. **Disable the amplitude control unless it is meaningful**
   - In the `state` handler in `controls.js`, enable `#sl-orbit-amplitude` only when:
     - `view_mode === "world"`
     - `orbit_mode === "oscillate"`
     - `orbit_enabled === true`
   - Otherwise set the native `disabled` state so it is both visually greyed out and non-interactive.

4. **Verify the existing scene transition behavior**
   - Confirm that entering Oscillate causes the existing `oscActive` rising-edge path to capture the current azimuth as the center point.
   - Confirm switching Continuous → Oscillate while already orbiting starts the wave from the current camera azimuth rather than jumping back to a previous position.
   - Confirm stopping and restarting oscillation re-centers around the azimuth where it was restarted.
   - Only change `scene.js` if this verification exposes an edge-state bug; the triangle-wave implementation itself should not need to be replaced.

5. **Add regression coverage**
   - `host/tests/test_web.py`
     - Add a combined `set_view` test covering `orbit=true`, `orbit_mode="oscillate"`, and amplitude in one request.
     - Assert the resulting `UiState`, persisted config, and `_state_message()` all agree.
   - `host/tests/test_static_ui.py`
     - Add a regression around the Oscillate control wiring so future changes cannot return to a mode-selection-only path that leaves orbit disabled.
     - Pin the amplitude-slider gating to oscillate/active World mode.
   - Keep the existing orbit-mode validation/range tests unchanged.

### Manual verification

1. Enter **World** view with Auto-orbit off.
2. Click **Oscillate**.
   - Camera should begin moving immediately.
3. Set amplitude to a small obvious value such as 10°.
   - Camera should reverse near ±10° around the azimuth where oscillation started.
4. Change amplitude while running.
   - The new limits should take effect without a camera jump.
5. Turn Auto-orbit off.
   - Camera should stop and the amplitude slider should disable.
6. Turn Auto-orbit back on while Oscillate remains selected.
   - Oscillation should restart centered on the current azimuth.
7. Select **Continuous**.
   - Continuous orbit should work and the amplitude slider should disable.
8. Switch to FPV/Mirror.
   - Orbit controls should remain disabled and the locked camera must not move.

### Acceptance criteria

- Selecting **Oscillate** in World view produces visible camera motion without requiring an additional hidden/unclear step.
- Oscillation reverses at approximately `±orbit_amplitude_deg` around its start azimuth.
- Turning Auto-orbit off immediately parks the camera.
- The amplitude slider is disabled whenever oscillation is not actively applicable.
- Continuous orbit behavior is unchanged.
- FPV/Mirror remain locked.
- Orbit mode, enabled state, speed, and amplitude continue to survive state echoes and persisted configuration.

## Implementation plan

I’d implement this as a one-time UI focus action when the server-confirmed source transitions into `view`, reusing the existing card-collapse machinery rather than adding separate visibility rules.

### 1. Centralize programmatic card collapse in `layout.js`

Refactor the existing collapse behavior in `host/src/roomscan/static/layout.js` into a helper that can be used both by:

- header/squircle clicks
- mode-driven UI changes

The helper should:

- add/remove `.collapsed`
- update `roomscan.card.<id>.collapsed` consistently
- refresh the squircle rail
- schedule/re-run layout

Expose a small public hook such as:

```js
window.__setCardCollapsed(cardId, collapsed)
````

This avoids `browser.js` directly manipulating classes/localStorage and getting out of sync with `layout.js`.

### 2. Apply the View focus policy on the source transition

In `host/src/roomscan/static/browser.js`, extend the existing `hub.on('state', ...)` handler.

Detect the actual transition:

```text
previous source != "view"
new source      == "view"
```

On that transition:

1. Enumerate cards using `[data-card-id]` rather than maintaining a brittle hard-coded list.
2. Collapse every card except `data-card-id="browser"`.
3. Explicitly expand `browser`.
4. Let the existing `browserCard.hidden` logic make the Captures card visible.
5. Trigger the normal relayout path.

Only do this on the transition into View — **not on every `state` message**. Otherwise a user who deliberately expands Sensors/View/etc. while browsing a capture would have it immediately collapsed again by the next server echo.

This naturally covers the current Stream, Sensors, IR Monitor, Device, View, Record, Playback, SLAM, Resources, Event Log, etc. cards and future cards that adopt `data-card-id`.

### 3. Reconcile the existing map-display auto-collapse

`browser.js` currently has `collapseForMapDisplay()`, which collapses the Captures card when View is showing `slam` or `detailed`.

Make sure that behavior does not immediately undo WEB-4 on the same Live → View state transition.

Change it so map auto-collapse only fires for a display transition **while already in View**, e.g.:

```text
previous source == "view"
current source  == "view"
display entered slam/detailed
```

Result:

* Clicking **View** always lands with Captures expanded.
* Afterward, switching the View display to SLAM/Detailed can retain the existing “get the browser out of the map” behavior.
* No source transition can produce an expand-then-collapse flicker.

### 4. Keep server state authoritative

Do not perform this immediately from the `#seg-source` click handler in `slam.js`.

That handler currently only sends:

```js
{ type: 'set_source', source: 'view' }
```

Keep that one-way state model intact. The card focus change should happen only after the server broadcasts `state.source === "view"`, matching the rest of the UI and keeping multiple tabs consistent with accepted server state.

### 5. Regression coverage

Add a headless-browser regression using the existing Chrome/Playwright workflow documented in `docs/web-ui-testing.md`.

Cover at least:

1. Start in Live with several cards expanded.
2. Click View and wait for the server `state` echo.
3. Assert:

   * `#browser-card` is visible.
   * `#browser-card` is **not** `.collapsed`.
   * every other `[data-card-id]` card is `.collapsed`.
   * squircle indicators match the card state.
4. Expand another card manually while still in View.
5. Allow another `state`/`session` update through and assert it stays expanded, proving the policy is transition-only.
6. Enter View while the selected display is SLAM/Detailed and verify Captures is still initially expanded.
7. Then change display while already in View and verify the existing map-display collapse behavior still works.

### Expected files

* `host/src/roomscan/static/layout.js`

  * reusable programmatic collapse helper
  * keep persistence/squircle/layout behavior centralized
* `host/src/roomscan/static/browser.js`

  * detect Live/Splat → View transition
  * apply View focus policy
  * tighten `collapseForMapDisplay()` transition condition
* headless web-UI regression alongside the existing browser verification tooling/tests

### Acceptance criteria

* Switching to **View** always presents an expanded **Captures** card.
* Every other card is minimized on that transition.
* The behavior is driven by the confirmed server state, not optimistic click state.
* Subsequent state messages do not continually force cards closed.
* Users can manually reopen cards after entering View.
* Existing SLAM/Detailed map-space behavior continues to work after the initial View landing.

## Implementation plan

Implement WEB-5 as client-side camera behavior, keeping the existing server-side view/follow state unchanged.

### 1. Add keyboard navigation to `scene.js`

Update `host/src/roomscan/static/scene.js` to track a set of currently pressed navigation keys:

- `W` / `S` — forward / backward
- `A` / `D` — left / right
- `Space` — ascend
- `Ctrl` or `C` — descend

Use `KeyboardEvent.code` (`KeyW`, `Space`, `ControlLeft`, etc.) so handling is independent of keyboard layout.

Keep keyboard navigation **World-view only**. FPV and Mirror are intentionally scanner-locked today and should retain that behavior.

### 2. Move the camera continuously in the render loop

Apply movement from `animate()` using its existing wall-clock `dt` rather than browser key-repeat events.

For each frame:

1. Derive camera forward with `camera.getWorldDirection()`.
2. Project forward onto the horizontal XZ plane so W/S do not change altitude.
3. Derive the horizontal right vector from forward and the existing `CAM_UP`.
4. Add the requested WASD + vertical directions and normalize diagonal movement.
5. Multiply by a single `NAV_SPEED_M_S` constant and `dt`.
6. Translate **both** `camera.position` and `controls.target` by the same delta.

Moving camera and target together preserves the user's existing OrbitControls zoom distance and viewing angle.

### 3. Temporarily suspend auto-follow without changing persisted state

Do not send `slam_opt` and do not toggle the Follow checkbox when navigation begins.

Instead, make the pressed-key set a temporary local override:

- While any navigation key is held, `trackTarget()` should ignore World-mode SLAM follow updates.
- When the final navigation key is released, remove the override.
- The next SLAM pose update can immediately call `trackTarget()` again if the existing server-owned `slam_follow` state is enabled.
- If Follow was already disabled, releasing the keys must not enable it.

This preserves the current one-way server-state architecture and avoids broadcasting a transient keyboard gesture to every connected tab.

### 4. Handle focus/lost-key edge cases

Prevent navigation from getting stuck when a key-up event is missed:

- Clear the pressed-key set on `window.blur`.
- Clear it when the document becomes hidden.
- Ignore navigation shortcuts when the active target is an input, select, textarea, or content-editable control.
- Prevent the browser's default Space/Ctrl behavior only when that key is actually being consumed for 3D navigation.

### 5. Keep auto-follow integration localized

No protocol or `web.py` change should be necessary.

`slam.js` already routes World-mode following through `sceneApi.trackTarget(...)`, so the temporary navigation override can live entirely inside `scene.js`. FPV/Mirror continue using `setSlamPose()` / `setFollowTarget()` unchanged.

### 6. Tests

Add coverage in `host/tests/test_static_ui.py` for the important structural invariants:

- all requested navigation key codes are registered;
- World tracking is suppressed while navigation is active;
- navigation translates camera and OrbitControls target together;
- blur/visibility cleanup clears held navigation state.

Then run the existing host test suite.

Also validate in the browser/headless UI:

1. World view: W/A/S/D moves relative to the current view.
2. Space and Ctrl/C move vertically.
3. Diagonal movement is not faster than single-axis movement.
4. Holding a key while SLAM Follow is enabled stops the camera being pulled back toward the scanner.
5. Releasing the final key resumes Follow automatically.
6. Follow remains off if it was off before navigation.
7. FPV/Mirror remain scanner-locked.
8. Typing/interacting with normal UI controls does not move the camera.
9. Losing browser focus while holding a key does not leave movement or follow suppression stuck.

### Acceptance criteria

- WASD + Space + Ctrl/C provide smooth, frame-rate-independent free-camera translation in World view.
- Camera framing/orbit angle is preserved while translating.
- Auto-follow is suspended only for the duration of active keyboard navigation and resumes after the last key is released.
- The server-side Follow setting is never changed as a side effect of navigation.
- FPV/Mirror behavior and mouse OrbitControls remain unchanged.

## Implementation plan — #101: View mode can display live data instead of the loaded capture

Issue: https://github.com/hellosamblack/lidar-roomscanner/issues/101  
Verified: open, `priority/now`, and **0 comments**.

### Diagnosis

The intended invariant is “View means a selected immutable capture.” Currently:

- `set_source(view)` leaves the live reader running while no capture is selected.
- Point cloud, IR, sensors, metrics, and SLAM consume shared state without a source-generation boundary.
- Cached frames and delayed reader callbacks can survive a live → capture transition.
- `/ws-mesh` is separate from `/ws`, so an already queued live mesh can arrive after the main socket announces View mode.

### Implementation

1. **Introduce a source generation**
   - Add a monotonically increasing generation to `SessionController`.
   - Increment it for every live/replay/capture switch.
   - Pass the captured generation into `_run_reader`.
   - Guard metrics, `SensorState.feed`, SLAM submission, and render-slot writes so callbacks from an obsolete reader are discarded.
   - Include the generation with render-slot entries so `_broadcaster` can reject stale frames.

2. **Reset source-owned state at the switch boundary**
   - Add complete source-reset methods to `SensorState` and `MetricsRegistry`; clear quaternion, environment, histories, rate meters, and render counters.
   - Reset the broadcaster’s `last_item`, packed point-cloud cache, orientation/jitter/elevation smoothers, and IR state when the generation changes.
   - Preserve genuinely host-wide state such as resource utilization and user preferences.

3. **Enforce View readiness in `web.py`**
   - Define one predicate requiring:
     - `ui.source == "view"`;
     - `controller.mode == "replay"`;
     - `selected_capture` matches `controller.replay_path`.
   - While View has no selected capture, show the browser but emit no point-cloud, IR, sensor, stream, or SLAM data.
   - Refuse SLAM/Detailed/Preview activation until the predicate is satisfied.
   - Gate every source-owned broadcaster branch on the active generation and readiness predicate.

4. **Add a client reset barrier**
   - Add `stream_generation` and `stream_ready` to the authoritative `state` message.
   - In `ws.js`, emit a local `stream_reset` before delivering state for a new generation.
   - Handle it in:
     - `scene.js`: clear point/surface draw ranges;
     - `slam.js`: clear mesh, trajectory, scanner pose, and detailed progress;
     - `ir.js`: clear the canvas and orientation state;
     - `sensors.js`: clear readings, gizmos, histories, and warning timers;
     - `hud.js`: clear source-specific Stream rates, drops, and gaps.
   - Keep the capture browser visible while `stream_ready` is false.

5. **Order the separate mesh channel**
   - Send a JSON `mesh_reset` barrier on `/ws-mesh` after any previously queued mesh for the old generation.
   - Teach `ws.js` to accept this text control frame on the mesh socket.
   - Do not cache or transmit meshes whose generation is no longer active.
   - Document the additive control message in `docs/web-protocol.md`; the binary mesh layout remains unchanged.

### Regression coverage

Add `host/tests/test_web_view_scope_e2e.py` using:

- a fake live source continuously producing recognizable depth, IR, IMU, and environment values;
- a capture fixture containing deliberately different values;
- delayed old-generation callbacks injected after the capture loads;
- the real server, WebSockets, and headless Chrome.

Verify independently that:

- **Point cloud:** geometry contains only capture depths.
- **SLAM:** pose, trajectory, and mesh derive only from capture frames.
- **Stream:** stream rows/rates identify only capture streams.
- **Sensors:** heading, orientation, pressure, and temperature match the capture.
- **IR monitor:** rendered pixel checksum matches the capture.
- Entering View without selecting a capture clears all five surfaces.
- Switching capture A → B never shows live data or stale A data after B’s reset barrier.
- Returning to Live restores normal live updates.

Also add focused unit tests for generation invalidation, state resets, View readiness, and mesh-reset ordering. Prove the end-to-end test by temporarily removing the generation guard and confirming that delayed live packets make it fail.

- Run the focused View-scope tests.
- Run the complete host pytest suite.
- Exercise Live → View browser → capture A → capture B → Live in headless Chrome.
- Capture screenshots for Point cloud, SLAM, Stream, Sensors, and IR.

## BUG-071 — `resolve_command()` never wired up `"standby"`, so `rig_command`/generic `cmd` can't send it

**Status:** open, not fixed (found incidentally, out of scope for the pass that found it) ·
**Area:** host/web · **Found by:** trying to exercise `SET_STANDBY` via `rig_command(name="standby",
...)` while verifying the 2026-08-03 auto-idle work, 2026-08-03.

`resolve_command()` (`web.py`, backs the generic inbound `{"type": "cmd", "name": ...}` message) maps
`ping`/`calib`/`reinit`/`usecase`/`period`/`exposure` to their `CommandCode`s and returns `None` —
"unknown/invalid cmd request" — for anything else. `"standby"` was never added, even though the wire
protocol fully supports it (`CommandCode.SET_STANDBY`, `RS_CMD_SET_STANDBY`) and the CLI tool
(`roomscan-ctl standby <0|1|2>`, `host/src/roomscan/control.py`) already parses it correctly
(`test_control_cli_parses_standby`). The web app's own `SET_STANDBY` traffic goes entirely through
the dedicated `set_idle` message → `_dispatch_standby()`, which never routes through
`resolve_command()`, so this gap was invisible until something tried to send `standby` as a generic
`cmd` — which is exactly what the `rig_command` MCP tool's own docstring claims is supported
(`"name is one of ping, calib, reinit, usecase, period, exposure, standby"`).

**Not fixed**: found while validating an unrelated feature (auto-idle activity accounting), and
`rig_set`/`set_idle`/the auto-idle machinery are all unaffected — this only blocks a *manual* generic
`cmd` standby request over `/ws`, e.g. via `rig_command`. Fix is a one-line addition to
`resolve_command()` (`if name == "standby": return CommandCode.SET_STANDBY, int(param), f"standby
{int(param)}"`), but wasn't made without a clearer picture of why the app deliberately built a
separate `set_idle` path instead of just using generic `cmd` here in the first place — worth checking
that history before adding the case, in case there was a reason (e.g. wanting persisted
enabled/level state that a bare `cmd` round-trip doesn't carry).

---

comments.body:
## Implementation plan

I’d fix this as a small host/web command-routing change and deliberately leave the existing `set_idle` / auto-idle machinery separate.

### 1. Add `standby` to the generic command resolver

In `host/src/roomscan/web.py`, extend `resolve_command()` with the missing mapping:

- `"standby"` → `CommandCode.SET_STANDBY`
- convert the supplied parameter to `int`, consistent with `period` / `exposure`
- preserve the numeric level in the command label, e.g. `standby 0`, `standby 1`, `standby 2`

Conceptually:

    if name == "standby":
        level = int(param)
        return CommandCode.SET_STANDBY, level, f"standby {level}"

This lets the existing generic `{"type":"cmd","name":"standby","param":...}` path use the same `CommandDispatcher` and ACK/log handling as every other generic command.

### 2. Keep generic `standby` separate from `set_idle`

Do **not** route this through the existing `set_idle` handler.

They serve different purposes:

- `cmd/standby` is a one-shot device command, equivalent to `roomscan-ctl standby <0|1|2>` and useful to `rig_command`.
- `set_idle` configures the web server's automatic idle policy (`idle_enabled` / `idle_level`), persists those preferences, manages debounce/activity state, and issues standby commands later through `_dispatch_standby()`.

A manual generic standby request therefore should not silently change or persist the user's auto-idle settings.

Also avoid trying to update `state.sensor_idled` optimistically from the generic command path: the dispatcher is asynchronous and the command can fail. The existing auto-idle bookkeeping should continue to describe commands issued by the auto-idle subsystem itself rather than pretending a manual command was acknowledged before the ACK arrives.

### 3. Add resolver regression coverage

Extend the existing `resolve_command` tests in `host/tests/test_web.py`.

Add a parameterized test covering all three protocol values:

- `standby 0` → `(CommandCode.SET_STANDBY, 0, "standby 0")`
- `standby 1` → `(CommandCode.SET_STANDBY, 1, "standby 1")`
- `standby 2` → `(CommandCode.SET_STANDBY, 2, "standby 2")`

Keep the existing unknown-command test to ensure unsupported names still return `None`.

### 4. Add one dispatch-level regression if the existing test harness makes it cheap

Exercise the generic inbound command path with:

    {"type": "cmd", "name": "standby", "param": 1}

and assert that the dispatcher receives:

    CommandCode.SET_STANDBY, 1, "standby 1"

This pins the actual BUG-071 failure mode rather than only testing the pure helper.

The test should not require hardware; mock/fake the dispatcher exactly as the existing web command tests do.

### 5. Protect the separate auto-idle behavior

Run the existing sensor-idle tests, especially those covering:

- persisted `idle_enabled` / `idle_level`
- `_dispatch_standby()`
- viewer leave/join auto-idle behavior
- wake behavior

No changes should be required in `set_idle`, `_dispatch_standby()`, or the browser idle UI.

### Verification

Run at minimum:

    pytest host/tests/test_web.py host/tests/test_sensor_idle.py

Then run the full host test suite.

For an end-to-end smoke test against a live rig, send:

    rig_command(name="standby", param=1)
    rig_command(name="standby", param=0)

and verify both commands receive normal `SET_STANDBY` ACKs instead of `unknown/invalid cmd request`.

### Expected files changed

- `host/src/roomscan/web.py`
- `host/tests/test_web.py`

No firmware or protocol changes should be necessary; `SET_STANDBY` already exists on the wire and is already supported by the CLI and the dedicated auto-idle path.

`corelib/include/rtabmap/core/Parameters.h:402-403`). A phone on a tripod adds **zero** nodes,
so a stationary sensor cannot contribute geometry or pose error to the map at all.

**What we do.** `Mapper.step` integrates every frame unconditionally at ~30 fps. There is no
displacement gate anywhere between the reader and `TsdfMap.integrate`.

**Why it matters here.** This is the zero-velocity constraint #101/BUG-069 says the reconstruction
lacks, expressed as a map-update gate rather than a detector — and unlike `StationarityGate`
(display-only, and requires <=0.3 deg/frame so it cannot fire during a pan) a displacement gate is
in the reconstruction path and is trivially correct. It also directly attacks BUG-067: on
`captures/imuTranslationError.bin` (tripod, true translation ~ the head's lever arm) the pipeline
reports 18-20 m of path at mean fitness 0.88. Frames that contribute no new viewpoint can only
contribute ICP noise.

Secondary benefit: fewer integrations per metre means slower TSDF block growth, which is upstream
of #111 (SLAM-2, mesh-extraction ceiling) and BUG-035.

**To explore.**
- Gate on the *pose delta since last integrated frame*, not on IMU rate — the source of the pose is
  the thing we are deciding to trust.
- Pick thresholds by matched ensembles over >=3 captures (tripod + both room circuits), per the
  `slam-ensemble` protocol; a single run cannot distinguish this from chaos.
- Decide what a gated frame still does: it should still update display/orientation and probably
  still feed ICP for pose continuity, just not `integrate()`. Those are separable and the
  answer may differ.
- Watch for the opposite failure: gating too aggressively starves frame-to-model tracking of
  recent geometry.

Related: #110 (SLAM-1), #112 (SLAM-3), BUG-067, BUG-069.

## Implementation plan

I’d implement this as a **TSDF integration gate only**: tracking/ICP continues on every usable frame, but the map is updated only after the pose has moved far enough from the last frame that was actually integrated.

### 1. Add configurable keyframe thresholds

In `host/src/roomscan/slam/config.py` and `Mapper.__init__`, add:

- `keyframe_linear_m`
- `keyframe_angular_deg`

Semantics:

- `0` disables that criterion.
- Both `0` preserves today's behavior exactly: every successfully tracked frame integrates.
- The first successfully tracked frame always integrates.
- With the gate enabled, integrate when **either** the translation or rotation from the last integrated pose exceeds its enabled threshold.

Start the validation sweep around RTAB-Map's mobile values:

- linear: `0.02 / 0.05 / 0.10 m`
- angular: `~1.7 / 2.9 / 5.7°` (`0.03 / 0.05 / 0.10 rad`)

Keep the shipped default disabled until the matched-capture results select a threshold.

### 2. Separate tracking state from map-keyframe state

`Mapper.step()` currently couples two operations:

1. `TsdfMap.integrate(...)`
2. advancing `_t_prev`

That coupling must be broken.

Add `_last_integrated_pose`, containing the full 4×4 pose of the last TSDF keyframe.

For every successfully tracked frame:

1. Run prediction, raycast and ICP exactly as today.
2. Apply barometer/ZUPT exactly as today.
3. Compare the resulting pose against `_last_integrated_pose`.
4. Integrate only when the keyframe gate passes.
5. **Always update `_t_prev` after successful tracking**, even when integration was skipped.
6. Update `_last_integrated_pose` only after a real `TsdfMap.integrate()`.

This is important: using `_t_prev` as the keyframe reference would make skipped frames stop advancing the tracking prior, turning a map-update optimization into a tracking behavior change.

No change should be required inside `TsdfMap`; the decision belongs in `Mapper`, where the pose history exists.

### 3. Make integration status explicit

Add a backward-compatible field to `FrameStep`:

`map_integrated: bool`

Set it:

- `True` when `TsdfMap.integrate()` actually ran.
- `False` on tracking-lost frames.
- `False` on successfully tracked frames suppressed by the keyframe gate.

Keep `integrate_ms = 0.0` on skipped frames.

Also maintain simple mapper counters for integrated vs. keyframe-skipped frames so capture sweeps can report the actual reduction rather than inferring it indirectly.

### 4. Fix worker mesh throttling

`host/src/roomscan/slam/worker.py` currently assumes:

`not step.tracking_lost == frame changed the TSDF`

That stops being true after this change.

Change `_frames_integrated` and mesh extraction scheduling to advance only when:

`step.map_integrated`

A gated frame should still immediately publish its fresh pose/trajectory/HUD data, but it should not trigger an expensive mesh extraction when the underlying map did not change.

### 5. Carry the flag through the remote backend

Update:

- `host/src/roomscan/slam/wire.py`
- `host/src/roomscan/slam/service.py`
- `host/src/roomscan/slam/remote.py`

Add optional `map_integrated` to the POSE message.

For compatibility with an older service, `RemoteSlamWorker` should interpret a missing field as:

`map_integrated = not tracking_lost`

because that is exactly the pre-keyframe behavior.

The mapper config itself already flows to the remote worker through the serialized mapper kwargs, so the new thresholds should use that existing path rather than adding another protocol mechanism.

### 6. Handle Detailed reconstruction explicitly

`DetailedSlamPreset.mapper_kwargs()` already builds on `SlamConfig.mapper_kwargs()`, so the knobs can propagate automatically.

Because these thresholds change reconstructed geometry, make the resolved Detailed thresholds part of the reconstruction preset/fingerprint if Detailed is going to use the gate. Do not let changing a keyframe threshold silently reuse a sidecar produced with a different integration policy.

### 7. Add regression tests

In `host/tests/test_slam_mapper.py`:

- First valid frame always integrates.
- Gate disabled -> every non-lost frame still integrates.
- A successfully tracked sub-threshold frame has `map_integrated == False`.
- `_t_prev` still advances when integration is skipped.
- `_last_integrated_pose` does not advance when integration is skipped.
- Several individually-small movements eventually exceed the displacement from the **last integrated pose** and create a new keyframe.
- Angular displacement can independently trigger integration.
- Tracking-lost frames neither integrate nor advance the integrated-pose reference.
- `SyntheticPan` remains tracked with the gate enabled.

In `host/tests/test_slam_worker.py`:

- A tracked-but-gated frame does not advance the mesh-extraction cadence.
- A subsequent integrated keyframe does.
- Pose publication still occurs on skipped frames.

In `host/tests/test_slam_wire.py` / service tests:

- `map_integrated` round-trips through a POSE message.
- Missing `map_integrated` retains old-service compatibility.
- Remote `FrameStep.map_integrated` matches the service result.

Keep the existing `test_mapper_kwargs_defaults_match_mapper_signature` and Detailed kwargs coverage tests passing so Live, CLI and Detailed cannot silently diverge.

### 8. Validate thresholds with matched capture ensembles

Run baseline + threshold candidates over at least:

1. `captures/imuTranslationError.bin` — tripod/null-translation case this issue is intended to attack.
2. `captures/coffeeRoomCircuitMnt.bin`
3. `captures/coffeeRoomCircuitNoMnt.bin`

Use identical perturbation seeds for every candidate.

Record:

- max excursion / stationary drift
- final closure error
- path length
- tracking-lost frames and longest lost streak
- fitness / RMSE
- integrated-frame count and percentage
- TSDF `blocks_used`
- total runtime / integration time

The gate is a win only if it materially reduces the tripod fabrication and integration/block growth **without increasing tracking loss or degrading room-circuit closure**. In particular, reject thresholds that save integrations by starving frame-to-model tracking of sufficiently recent geometry.

Once a threshold wins across the matched ensembles, make that the default for Live and Detailed; otherwise leave the feature available but disabled and record the negative result.

## Implementation plan

### Design

Keep Open3D’s existing marching-cubes implementation, but run it against spatially partitioned temporary VoxelBlockGrids:

1. Read active block coordinates from the source TSDF.
2. Partition them into fixed spatial chunks with a one-block halo.
3. Copy only each chunk’s TSDF, weight, and color attributes into a temporary CPU grid.
4. Extract each chunk below the 250k-block crash ceiling.
5. Keep triangles owned by that chunk, concatenate the results, weld boundary vertices, remove duplicate/degenerate triangles, and recompute normals.

This preserves current Open3D geometry and color semantics without adding another meshing dependency.

### Code changes

- [ ] Add `host/src/roomscan/slam/chunked_mesher.py`.

  - Snapshot active block keys once.
  - Transfer voxel attributes to CPU one chunk at a time.
  - Guarantee every temporary grid remains safely below `_MAX_SAFE_EXTRACT_BLOCKS`.
  - Support negative block coordinates and sparse rooms.
  - Return the existing host-resident `o3d.t.geometry.TriangleMesh` type.

- [ ] Update `host/src/roomscan/slam/tsdf.py`.

  - Split extraction-limit failures from integration/rehash capacity failures.
  - Add an extraction strategy to `TsdfMap.mesh()`:
    - `open3d`: existing guarded behavior.
    - `auto`: existing extractor below the ceiling, chunked extraction above it.
  - Leave `point_cloud()` unchanged unless a demonstrated caller also needs chunking.
  - Preserve the current default so live SLAM cannot unexpectedly start a long CPU extraction.

- [ ] Update `host/src/roomscan/slam/mapper.py`.

  - Forward the selected mesh strategy to `TsdfMap`.

- [ ] Update `host/src/roomscan/slam/showcase.py`.

  - Continue using fast Open3D extraction for intermediate Detailed previews.
  - Once the map exceeds the ceiling, stop attempting intermediate extraction, retain the last good preview, and continue integrating frames.
  - Use `auto` for the final mesh so the build completes through the chunked path.
  - Keep integration/rehash failures terminal and preserve the “never commit a partial sidecar” behavior.

- [ ] Update `host/src/roomscan/slam/cli.py`.

  - Use automatic chunked extraction for the CLI’s final mesh output as well.

- [ ] Re-enable the 5 mm Detailed preset only after the full-room validation gate passes.

  - Measure the complete 5 mm active-block count first.
  - Preallocate sufficient GPU capacity to avoid Open3D’s destructive rehash path when it fits safely.
  - Otherwise expose a Detailed-only CPU-device setting; chunked extraction fixes meshing capacity, but it must not conceal a separate TSDF integration-capacity failure.

### Tests

- [ ] Partitioning tests covering negative coordinates, empty chunks, halos, and the per-chunk block ceiling.
- [ ] Small-map parity test comparing standard and chunked extraction bounds, colors, and surface distance.
- [ ] Plane/corner fixtures crossing chunk boundaries, asserting no cracks, duplicate triangles, or degenerate faces.
- [ ] Lower the ceiling in a unit test so a small synthetic map exercises the chunked fallback without allocating 250k blocks.
- [ ] Verify `PostProcessWorker` continues processing after intermediate extraction reaches the ceiling and performs one final chunked extraction.
- [ ] Verify live `SlamWorker` retains its current last-good-mesh freeze behavior.
- [ ] Verify a failed final extraction still produces no PLY/TUM/manifest commit.

### Full-room acceptance gate

Run `DebugCapB1.bin` at 5 mm and require:

- all 4,808 frames are processed;
- active blocks exceed the old 250k ceiling;
- no segfault, CUDA illegal access, or unsafe rehash;
- a non-empty, reloadable PLY and current manifest are written;
- chunk peak memory remains bounded independently of total map size;
- seams are absent under boundary-edge and nearest-surface checks;
- a prefix below 250k blocks agrees with normal Open3D extraction within a small fraction of one voxel.

The 10 mm default should remain in place until this gate passes; then changing it back to 5 mm will intentionally invalidate older Detailed sidecars through the existing preset fingerprint.

## Implementation plan

I’d implement this as **bounded local relocalization after sustained tracking loss**, rather than a full global/loop-closure system.

### Current failure mode

`Mapper.step()` currently does the right thing for an isolated bad frame:

1. Predict pose from the current SFLP rotation + the last good translation.
2. Raycast the TSDF from that pose.
3. Run ICP.
4. If the normal correspondence radius fails, `register_escalating()` retries once at `icp_retry_dist`.
5. If that also fails, mark the frame lost, skip integration, and leave `_t_prev` unchanged.

The problem is step 5 after a multi-frame outage. Translation remains frozen at the last good position while the scanner may continue moving, so every subsequent raycast starts farther from reality. There is currently no mechanism that can search its way back onto the existing map.

### Proposed approach

#### 1. Add an explicit relocalization state machine

In `host/src/roomscan/slam/mapper.py`, track:

- consecutive post-bootstrap lost frames
- whether relocalization is active
- the current search cursor / candidate set
- an optional provisional recovered pose
- attempt / success / failure counters

Keep the existing `register_escalating()` path unchanged for ordinary tracking. Relocalization only activates after a sustained lost streak (initially ~3–5 frames; tune from the DC-C fixture).

#### 2. Add a bounded translation search

Create something like:

`host/src/roomscan/slam/relocalization.py`

The SFLP quaternion already gives us a strong current orientation prior, so the first implementation should search **translation**, not arbitrary 6-DoF poses.

Generate translation candidates around the last known-good `_t_prev`:

- search primarily in world X/Z (Y is the vertical axis in the current Open3D CV-world convention)
- keep only a small vertical band around the last position / barometric estimate
- expand outward in rings
- coarse search first, then refine around a promising candidate
- cap the number of candidates evaluated per frame so recovery cannot stall the SLAM worker

Starting values to validate, not hard requirements:

- max horizontal radius: ~1.5–2.0 m
- coarse spacing: ~0.25–0.5 m
- vertical band: ~±0.25 m
- candidate budget: ~4–8 evaluations per SLAM iteration

#### 3. Evaluate candidates with the existing TSDF, without extracting the whole map

For each candidate translation:

1. Combine the candidate translation with the **current IMU/SFLP rotation**.
2. Raycast the existing TSDF at that candidate pose using the current depth frame as `depth_hint`.
3. Reject candidates whose raycast produces too few model points.
4. Run the existing ICP implementation against that raycast, with a relocalization-specific correspondence radius.
5. Rank passing candidates using fitness/RMSE.

Do **not** build relocalization around `TsdfMap.point_cloud()` or full mesh extraction. The repository already has a known Open3D extraction ceiling; candidate raycasts keep this bounded to the current frustum and avoid coupling SLAM-3 to that separate problem.

Use a stricter acceptance gate than ordinary tracking. Initial values can be around fitness >= 0.6 / RMSE <= 0.03 m, then tune from real captures.

Also reject ambiguous results where two spatially different candidates score essentially the same rather than guessing in a repetitive room.

#### 4. Require confirmation before modifying the map

A coarse relocalization hit should **not immediately integrate into the TSDF**.

Instead:

1. Store the winning pose as provisional.
2. Use it as the prediction for the next valid frame.
3. Require normal, tight ICP to succeed from that pose.
4. Only after confirmation:
   - commit the recovered translation to `_t_prev`
   - resume TSDF integration
   - reset the lost streak/search state
   - increment the relocalization-success counter

If confirmation fails, throw away the provisional pose and continue searching.

This is important because a false relocalization is much worse than remaining visibly tracking-lost: one incorrect integration can permanently corrupt the TSDF.

#### 5. Keep normal tracking behavior untouched

When tracking is healthy:

- no candidate search
- no extra raycasts
- no changes to the current ICP path
- no changes to TSDF integration
- no added hot-path cost besides a lost-streak counter

The existing one-frame `icp_retry_dist` recovery remains the first line of defense.

### Configuration

Add a minimal set of knobs to `host/src/roomscan/slam/config.py` and mirror them through all Mapper construction paths:

- `relocalize_enabled`
- `relocalize_after_frames`
- `relocalize_radius_m`
- `relocalize_candidates_per_frame`

Keep finer search/scoring constants private initially. We should tune those from the real fixture before turning them into permanent configuration surface.

Make sure the new Mapper kwargs flow through:

- live `SlamRunner`
- CLI / Detailed SLAM
- `slam/service.py` remote worker path

### Observability

Expose at least:

- relocalization attempts
- relocalization successes
- relocalization failures/exhaustions
- whether the current pose is provisional/relocalizing

If these are included in the remote SLAM status, update `slam/wire.py`, `slam/remote.py`, `slam/service.py`, and their protocol tests together so local and remote backends report the same state.

### Tests

Add focused unit tests for the search machinery:

- candidate generation expands outward deterministically
- X/Z search uses the correct world axes
- candidate count is bounded per iteration
- search resets cleanly after success/failure
- no duplicate candidates

Extend `host/tests/test_slam_mapper.py` with:

- a normal tracked sequence never invokes relocalization
- a post-bootstrap lost streak triggers relocalization
- failed candidates leave `_t_prev` and the TSDF untouched
- a provisional candidate is **not** integrated immediately
- a successful next-frame confirmation commits the pose and resumes integration
- failed confirmation returns to search
- invalid/too-sparse depth frames do not produce false recovery
- exhausting the search leaves tracking lost rather than accepting a bad pose
- the relocalization path never calls full `TsdfMap.point_cloud()` extraction

Add/update config and local/remote plumbing tests where the new settings/telemetry pass through.

### Validation / acceptance criteria

Replay the **DC-C tracking-kill fixture referenced by this issue**.

Baseline should reproduce the sustained lost tail. With relocalization enabled:

- tracking reacquires after the outage
- `tracking_stats(...).died` becomes false
- trailing/longest lost runs are bounded to the outage + search time
- TSDF integration resumes after confirmed recovery
- the recovered trajectory does not contain a large discontinuity inconsistent with the physical capture

Regression-test clean captures as well:

- captures with no sustained tracking failure should perform **zero relocalization attempts**
- their trajectory/map output should remain unchanged apart from any newly reported counters
- normal SLAM latency should remain unchanged
- the BUG-067 stationary/pan cases should not accidentally trigger relocalization when tracking itself is still valid

Finally, test an intentionally unrecoverable displacement outside the configured search radius. The correct behavior there is to remain `tracking_lost`, not to snap to a superficially similar part of the room.

### Suggested implementation order

1. Add relocalization search/candidate primitives + unit tests.
2. Add lost-streak/provisional-pose state to `Mapper`.
3. Integrate bounded candidate raycasts + ICP scoring.
4. Add next-frame confirmation and integration guard.
5. Add configuration/plumbing.
6. Add observability.
7. Replay DC-C and tune the search radius, spacing, acceptance gate, and ambiguity threshold from measured results.
8. Run the clean-capture regression set before enabling it by default.

**Original title:** officeFullScanAug6.bin forks near frame ~979: the ceiling drops below the previously established height, and Detailed SLAM reconstructs a separate set of rooms

## BUG-084 — SLAM forks into a second, vertically displaced set of rooms near frame 979

**Date filed:** 2026-08-06  
**Area:** host/slam  
**Status:** open (reproducible from the supplied capture; root cause unknown)

## Symptom

`captures/officeFullScanAug6.bin` contains a catastrophic SLAM discontinuity at
approximately frame **979**. The mapper places the ceiling substantially lower than the
ceiling it had already detected earlier in the scan. The resulting map is not merely
slightly warped: the Detailed SLAM reconstruction shows a separate, internally coherent
set of rooms rather than the same room layout continued from the earlier trajectory.

The ceiling-height jump and the second-room-set result indicate a map fork, relocalization
failure, or similarly terminal pose discontinuity. They should be investigated together;
the Detailed result independently exposes the failure even if the live preview makes the
transition difficult to see.

## Reproduction

1. Load `captures/officeFullScanAug6.bin`.
2. Run SLAM through the capture, including frames around 979.
3. Compare the ceiling height before and after the discontinuity.
4. Run the same capture through Detailed SLAM and compare its room layout with the map
   established before frame 979.

## Expected behavior

The ceiling should remain at the previously established physical height, and the scan
should continue in the same world/map. If tracking confidence is insufficient to maintain
that estimate, SLAM should reject or clearly flag the transition rather than silently
creating a second set of rooms at a different elevation.

## Impact

The capture's reconstruction is unusable across the discontinuity. A visually plausible
but vertically displaced map can contaminate room dimensions and any downstream mesh or
measurement, while the separate Detailed room set makes the failure look like valid new
geometry rather than an explicit tracking loss.

## Investigation notes

- The first reported onset is around frame 979; determine the exact last-good and first-bad
  frames during analysis.
- Compare raw and fused orientation priors, ICP fitness/correspondences, tracking-lost
  gates, barometer authority, and pose increments across the boundary.
- Check whether the live and Detailed paths diverge at the same frame or whether one path
  is masking an earlier pose error.
- Do not infer a physical second room set from the Detailed mesh until the pose trajectory
  has been checked for a discontinuity.

## Related issues

- BUG-067: SLAM can fabricate large motion while reporting healthy tracking.
- BUG-068: ill-conditioned translation solves were accepted by an ineffective guard.
- BUG-070: SLAM behavior depends on the world-frame heading prior.

**Original title:** Reported drift is not invariant to a physically null relabelling of compass heading: a constant graft_yaw offset swings a stationary capture's reported displacement from 0.81 ± 0.53 m (0°) to 2.89 ± 0.14 m (90°), repeatably. This is why Live SLAM (mag-grafted prior) reads ~4× worse than Detailed (raw SFLP prior) on the same bytes. Still open 2026-08-06: the accel ZUPT (BUG-069) tightens each heading's run-to-run variance (now deterministic, no longer bistable — 0.104 at 0°, 2.44 ± 0.36 at 90°) but does NOT remove the across-heading dependence; not root-caused. Clue: the fabrication appears anchored in the world/CV frame (its coherence rotates with the graft), so suspect the prior yaw's interaction with the NN search / raycast viewpoint

## BUG-070 — reported drift changes by 2 m under a physically null change of compass heading

**Status:** anomaly (reproducible, measured, not root-caused) · **Area:** host/slam · **Found by:**
isolating why Live SLAM and Detailed disagree on BUG-067's capture, 2026-08-02.

Live SLAM feeds `sensor.fused_quat()` (SFLP with a magnetometer heading graft, +56.8° on this
capture); Detailed feeds the raw SFLP quat via `_load_frames`. Live reads ~4× worse. The obvious
explanation — that the mag correction *wanders*, which it does, ±2–3° over the run — **is wrong**:
a **frozen constant** graft is just as bad (1.81 ± 0.77 m vs the live 1.69 ± 0.52 m).

`graft_yaw` is a pure heading change; verified numerically that boresight tilt and the CV-world
up-component are preserved to machine precision under grafts of 45/90/180°, and the
`T_WORLD_TO_CV @ R @ T_CV_TO_BODY` sandwich carries it correctly. So a constant graft relabels
compass directions and changes no physics. Yet, sweeping it (n=4 each, max excursion):

```
  0° 0.81 ± 0.53    15° 1.28 ± 0.89    30° 0.81 ± 0.32    45° 1.42 ± 0.61
 57° 1.59 ± 0.70    60° 1.37 ± 0.62    75° 2.21 ± 0.62    90° 2.89 ± 0.14   180° 2.84 ± 0.17
```

**What it is not.** Not the voxel lattice: a 90° rotation about world up maps the cubic lattice onto
itself, so 0/90/180 would agree, and they do not. Not the barometer: `baro_authority=0` gives 2.77
at 90° vs 3.02 with it on. Not a tracking failure: 0 lost frames, mean fitness 0.882–0.885 at both
0° and 90°.

**What it looks like.** The 0° and 90° runs track *identically* (distance-from-origin within 0.1 m)
until t ≈ 88 s, then 90° slips 0.83 → 2.98 m across the BUG-068 window while 0° does not. So heading
is not a systematic cause — it biases which side of a **bistable** marginal event the run lands on.
That a null relabelling can decide a 2 m outcome is the honest measure of how unstable this
translation estimate is (BUG-067), and it means **any single-run comparison across captures with
different headings is confounded** — a sharper version of the "score ensembles, not single runs"
rule from BUG-037.

**BUG-068 did NOT fix it** — the prediction first written here was wrong, and is corrected rather
than deleted. Re-running the sweep with the shipped conditioning cap (n=4, max excursion):

```
   heading      cap 0 (pre-fix)     cap 20 (shipped)
       0°      0.814 +/- 0.529      0.469 +/- 0.079
      45°      1.421 +/- 0.605      1.454 +/- 0.706
      57°      1.591 +/- 0.699      0.926 +/- 0.417
      90°      2.887 +/- 0.141      2.107 +/- 0.540
     180°      2.844 +/- 0.170      2.409 +/- 0.605
```

The cap stabilises the 0° case (spread 0.529 → 0.079) and does nothing for the heading dependence
itself: 45° is unchanged and 90° is still 4.5× the 0° result. So this is a **second, independent**
defect, not a downstream symptom of BUG-068. Still not root-caused; recorded so a future session
does not have to rediscover it, and so nobody assumes the conditioning fix covered it.

**The accel ZUPT (BUG-069) did NOT fix it either (2026-08-06).** The graft sweep re-run with the
shipped default config (ZUPT on), n=8 max excursion:

```
   0°  0.104 +/- 0.016      45°  0.924 +/- 0.755
  90°  2.443 +/- 0.363     180°  2.546 +/- 0.130
```

ZUPT collapses the run-to-run spread *within* a heading (0° sd 0.079 → 0.016; note 90° and 180° are
now TIGHT too — 0.363, 0.130 — the estimate is deterministic per heading, not bistable) but the
across-heading swing is intact: 90°/180° still sit at ~2.5 m, ~24× the 0° result. So this is now
better described as a **systematic heading dependence**, not a bistable coin-flip — a null world-Z
relabel of the prior deterministically moves the fabricated trajectory by metres. That the ZUPT's
coherence veto holds at 0° but not at 90° suggests the fabricated pan drift's *direction* (hence its
coherence) rotates with the graft, which is itself the clue: the fabrication is anchored to something
in the world/CV frame, not the body. Prime remaining suspects to test next: the interaction of the
world-frame prior yaw with the NN correspondence search / raycast viewpoint, and whether the
per-frame fabricated increment is coherent-in-world (a graft rotates it toward or away from the
veto's coherence axis). **Still open, still not root-caused**; confounds any single-run comparison
across captures (or Live-vs-Detailed on one capture) with different headings.

**Original title:** Multi-second whole-group frame loss on the multi-room captures — 2.29% / 4.28% / 9.35% of RAW frames lost while byte-clean and 0 CRC, in outages up to 215 frames (7.1 s). Cost DC-B take 2 a 628-frame (21.2 s) tracking collapse. Recurring 63-frame quantum in all three takes; not RF range (the bridge rides on the scanner, never roamed, signal > 80%)

## BUG-049 — Multi-second whole-group frame loss on the multi-room captures

**Status:** open · **Area:** host/transport · **Found:** 2026-07-31, scoring DC-B

The three DC-B takes are **byte-perfect** — 0 CRC failures, 0 bytes skipped, `clean: true` — while
missing large numbers of frames the device demonstrably sent:

| take | duration | RAW loss | whole-group | fragment-only | worst outage |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DebugCapB1` | 163 s | **2.29%** (113/4933) | 72 | 46 | 63 frames = 2.1 s @ 37.3 s |
| `DebugCapB2` | 165 s | **4.28%** (214/5004) | 139 | 86 | 73 = 2.4 s @ 5.8 s; 63 @ 136.3 s |
| `DebugCapB3` | 181 s | **9.35%** (512/5474) | 456 | 69 | **215 = 7.1 s @ 66.2 s**; 153 = 5.1 s @ 162.6 s |
| *`coffeeRoomCircuitNoMnt`* | 66 s | 0.15% | **0** | 4 | 1 frame |

**The device emitted them.** Sequence numbers advance continuously at a steady **30.29 fps** (seq span
÷ elapsed `t_us`) straight across the gaps, so these were lost between board and file. There are **zero
EVENT frames** in any take — the firmware never noticed.

**Two distinct mechanisms**, separated by `capture_analyze`'s new continuity census:
1. **Whole-group outages** — the seq is absent from streams 9/10/11/13 *and* 7, i.e. the 20-byte
   IMU_QUAT datagram vanished alongside the ~15 KB RAW one. Not bandwidth, not fragmentation.
   CALIB spacing degrades to 64/128/256 where it should be uniformly 64.
2. **RAW-only fragment loss** — 46/86/69 frames where only the ~11-fragment RAW datagram was lost.
   This is the BUG-041/BUG-042 neighbourhood and is present at low rate on *every* capture.

**Cost to SLAM, measured.** `DebugCapB2`'s 628-frame (21.2 s) tracking collapse begins at **t = 8.26 s**;
its transport outage ran **5.81 → 8.19 s**. Tracking died within ~70 ms of the hole ending and stayed
dead 21.2 s. This is the open "no relocalization" hole, quantified: SLAM is frame-to-model, so after a
2.4 s gap the pose prior is stale and ICP cannot re-register. **A bad 2.4 seconds cost 21 seconds.**
Timing matters more than length — `DebugCapB1`'s comparable 63-frame outage at t = 37.3 s cost it
**zero** lost frames, because by then there was a mature model to re-register against.

**What it is NOT.** Not RF range: the Wi-Fi bridge is permanently mounted on the scanner with a patch
cable, so its link endpoints never separate; the owner confirms it never roamed and signal stayed
above 80% (owner, 2026-07-31). Not block-grid saturation: re-running B2 at `block_count=500000`
gives byte-identical results with `blocks_used` unchanged at 154469, so 160000 was never limiting
(knob confirmed applied via the report's `block_count` field).

**What discriminates the remaining candidates.** The loss correlates with **walking**, not duration —
`DebugCapE` is 147 s, nearly as long as B1, recorded the same session, and has 3 whole-group losses.
A **63-frame (2.08 s) outage recurs in all three takes**, which is a quantum, not the continuous
distribution RF fading produces. Leading candidates: (a) Ethernet patch-cable link bounce — the one
hop that physically flexes, and link-down plus auto-negotiation is ~1–3 s, matching the quantum;
(b) background roaming scans on the bridge, which take the radio off-channel to *evaluate* candidates
without ever losing signal or roaming; (c) a stall in the firmware's slot-FIFO TX pacer (BUG-041),
which would block all streams together.

**Next step (owner action).** Record ~3 minutes stationary, flexing the patch cable at the connectors
partway through. If the outages follow the cable it is (a); if a still, untouched 3-minute capture
still shows them it is (b) or (c). Do it with the Drops/Gaps HUD visible — BUG-040 fixed those rows,
and BUG-042's counters separate reorder from loss, but none of that is stored in the capture file, so
it has to be read live.

**Instrument gap this exposed.** `capture_analyze` called all three takes `clean: true`, because it
only ever checked CRC and resync. It now reports a `continuity` block; `clean` and
`continuity.complete` are deliberately separate properties.

## Symptom

`ui_screenshot(width=…, height=…)` does not resize the browser viewport. Passing
`width=1100, height=560` and then `width=820, height=700` returned images that were
unchanged from the default framing, and `ui_eval("window.innerWidth")` /
`window.innerHeight` still reported **1600 x 1000** after both calls.

## Why it matters

`docs/web-ui-testing.md` prescribes verifying UI work at three narrow sizes —
`1280x800`, `1100x560`, `820x700` — for exactly the constrained-layout bugs where
narrowness is the failure condition. With these parameters inert, a session that
follows the documented procedure gets a **pass that means nothing**: same viewport,
same result, three times over, reported as three sizes covered. That is the
"invariant-preserving check verifies nothing" failure mode from AGENTS.md, but in the
tooling rather than in the code under test.

Found while verifying #103 (a clipped-out-of-the-card action drawer), where narrow
viewports were one of the acceptance conditions. Worked around there by starving the
card's height via the other dock cards instead — a real in-app squeeze, but not the
same thing as a narrow window, so #103's narrow-viewport row is genuinely unverified.

## Expected

Either the parameters set the Playwright viewport (`page.set_viewport_size`) before
shooting, or — if they are only meant to size the returned image — the docstring says
so and a separate `viewport`/`ui_viewport` control exists, since resizing is what the
testing doc actually asks for.

## Reproduction

```
ui_screenshot(width=1100, height=560)
ui_eval("(() => ({w: window.innerWidth, h: window.innerHeight}))()")
# -> {"w": 1600, "h": 1000}
```

## Notes

- `docs/web-ui-testing.md` now warns about this inline (landed with #103) — that note
  should be reduced to a pointer here once fixed.
- Worth checking the same question for `height` on the raw-CDP fallback path and for
  `host/tools/web_ui_shot.py`, which takes the same two arguments.

**Original title:** The GIL-starvation metric under-reports precisely when starvation is total — summed tick lateness over wall time falls toward zero as blocking approaches 100%, because the watchdog thread stops being scheduled at all (1 tick landed of ~2186 due read as "10.3% starved"). slam_icp_bench.py fixed with tick_share; slam_stall_profile.py still to do

## BUG-063 — the GIL-starvation metric under-reports precisely when starvation is total

**Status:** open (measured, one instrument fixed, one not) · **Area:** host/tools
(`slam_stall_profile.py`; `slam_icp_bench.py` already corrected) · **Found by:** the item 4 matched
CUDA ICP study, 2026-08-02, when a variant that visibly froze the process reported a *better*
starvation figure than stages that ran fine.

**The defect.** Both watchdog-based instruments compute starvation as **summed tick lateness over
wall time**. That construction is self-defeating: if the measured code holds the GIL continuously,
the watchdog thread barely gets scheduled, so there are almost no lateness samples to sum, and the
metric falls toward zero exactly as blocking approaches total.

**Measured.** Over a 10.93 s `gpu_translation` stage the watchdog landed **1 tick where ~2186 were
due**, and that single tick was 2998.9 ms late. The stage reported **"10.3% starvation"** — better
than stages that were genuinely healthy. Its true behaviour: whole-process freezes of 598.7 /
1626.8 / 2998.9 / 3981.6 ms, while **no single `register()` call exceeded 9 ms**.

**The fix, where applied.** `slam_icp_bench.py` reports **`tick_share` = ticks landed / ticks due**,
which degrades in the right direction:

| Variant | `tick_share` | ticks / due | worst stall | (legacy) starved % |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `translation` (shipped) | 0.953 | 1470 / 1542 | 2.0 ms | 4.7% |
| `6dof` | 0.989 | 1334 / 1349 | 0.2 ms | 1.1% |
| `gpu_translation` | **0.058** | 127 / 2209 | **3981.6 ms** | 66.7% |
| `translation_cpu_nns` | 0.951 | 1553 / 1632 | 4.2 ms | 4.9% |

**Still to do.** `host/tools/slam_stall_profile.py` computes starvation the same way and has the
same blind spot. **Its published numbers are not in doubt** — BUG-060's 11.9% vs 94.3% comparison
had ample ticks in both regimes, so the sum was well-sampled — but it should gain `tick_share`
before it is next used to clear a change, because the one situation it cannot currently see is the
one it exists to catch.

**Why this matters beyond the metric.** A low starvation reading is used as evidence that a change
is safe for `roomscan-web`, whose asyncio loop, reader thread and broadcaster all need the GIL. An
instrument that reads *healthy* under total blocking would have waved through exactly the
BUG-060/BUG-061 failure mode. Generalises the repo's standing lesson one level down: a native call's
wall time is not its blocking cost — and here even the starvation *percentage* was not its blocking
cost. Pair any "it didn't starve" claim with the number of samples the claim rests on.
